text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomy“We Will Find a Graviton Before We Find Dark Matter” A quantum information scientist on the hunt for the elemental mediator of gravity and why AI can’t solve physics problems creativelyKFBy Kristen French2:00 PM CDT on October 30, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleIgor Pikovski recently decided to tackle one of the holy grails of physics: discovering the quantum soul of gravity. “It's the biggest mystery of physics,” says the Stevens Institute of Technology quantum information scientist. Quantum physics was formulated more than a century ago by the collective efforts of many scientists, including Albert Einstein, Max Planck, and Niels Bohr, to explain some puzzling experimental results, and it has been an active field of inquiry ever since.We’ve come to understand that quantum physics can explain all kinds of strange effects in the universe. In fact, it can describe almost everything—except gravity. Many scientists have attempted to ferret out how gravity and quantum physics intersect, using string theory, for example, or theories of everything, says Pikovski. “It’s a very mathematical, speculative field where we don’t have answers yet,” says Pikovski.READ MORE: What Physicists Have Been MissingSubscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
